name: Museum of the Home
summary: A free museum about domestic life, in former eighteenth-century almshouses on Kingsland Road. Its displays include living rooms drawn from real London homes spanning 1600 to now.

accessibility.notes: The Geffrye Street entrance has 15 steps; the central and north gates have ramps and the south gate has none. Manual wheelchairs can be borrowed but not booked. Staff help is needed to reach the first-floor Collections Display. Child-sized ear-defenders and sensory backpacks are free to borrow.

cost.notes: Entry to the museum is free with no booking needed. Ticketed events must be booked online in advance.

age_policy: Unaccompanied children under 12 may be refused entry.

evidence.quote: We are the only museum of the home in the world, a place to learn how we have lived in the past, explore how we live today, and talk about how we can live better together.
Housed in a set of Grade I-listed eighteenth-century almshouses
a sequence of typical middle-class living rooms based on real London homes dating from 1600 to the present
Entrance is free and you do not need to book in advance.
formerly known as the Geffrye Museum after their patron
There is step-free access to all our galleries.
There is an accessible toilet suitable for wheelchair users in the reception area and two further accessible toilets across the museum.
There is an induction loop at Reception in the Welcome Area.
There are 15 steps from Geffrye Street to the main entrance.
At the central and north gates, ramps lead from the pavement down to a smooth and level path. The south gate does not have ramped access
You can borrow a manual wheelchair for use in our galleries and gardens.
You can’t book a wheelchair in advance.
To access the Collections Display on the first floor, please ask a member of our team for assistance.
Child-sized ear-defenders and backpacks filled with sensory toys are available to borrow from Reception during your visit, at no cost.
If you are attending a ticketed event, you must book a ticket in advance online from the event page.
We reserve the right to refuse admittance to any unaccompanied child under the age of 12.
the place to explore and debate what home means
